newsitem.title: USA: Dow Corning seeks potential breast implant claims.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning seeks potential breast implant claims.

text.p: Dow Corning Corp. on Thursday opened its bankruptcy court-approved programme to notify people who may have a claim against it because of their use of its breast implants.
Dow Corning, which had no estimate how many people might file claims, said the court-ordered deadline for filing a claim was next Jan. 15.
It said that potential claimants who did not file by that deadline may forever be barred from making a claim.
Thousands of women fitted with the silicone implants have claimed to become ill with connective tissue diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis.

Dow Corning and other implant makers had been named defendants in a class action law suit, but when a settlement was reached, many of the recipients of the implants dropped out and filed individual cases against Dow.
Facing possibly thousands of indiviudal trials, Dow Corning, jointly owned by a subsidary of Dow Chemical Co. and Corning Inc., filed for bankruptcy May 15.
Dow Corning said at a news conference that the effort to seek possible claimants was a step in the court's effort to resolve claims against the company.
Company spokeswoman Barie Carmichael said, however, that "whether the claim will be disputed, allowed or disallowed, will be determined at a later date."

She said Dow Corning would try to reach potential claimants through television and print advertising in the United States and foreign countries were its products were sold from the early 1960s until taken off the market in 1992.
In addition to breast implants, the company was also seeking claims from people with other types of implants, such as hip, knee, chin, joint, toe, nasal, penile and testicular.
